options: The underlying dictionary entry for a field
Which columns a list shows, and in what left-to-right order
Which records satisfy the list's underlying filter
Whether a table can be extended by another table
questions.explain: List Layout is a display-only configuration — it changes what columns show, never which rows qualify for the list.

questions.q: Why can two people looking at "the same" Incident list see different columns?
options: They are actually looking at two different tables
List views cannot be named or saved in ServiceNow
A table can have multiple named list views, and which one a user sees can depend on role or their own selection
One of them has more incident records than the other
questions.explain: Named list views like "Default view" and "Service Desk view" are separate saved column configurations on the identical underlying records.

questions.q: What happens to the underlying records when you Group By a column?
options: The list's filter conditions are permanently changed
Nothing — the records are only clustered and displayed differently, none are added or removed
Records matching the grouped value are deleted
The table's dictionary entries are rewritten
questions.explain: Group By, like sorting, only reorganizes how the same result set is presented — it doesn't filter or alter records.

questions.q: What can the right-click context menu on a list cell do?
options: Permanently delete the table
Change the table's base class in the task hierarchy
Rewrite the sys_dictionary entry for that field
Offer quick actions like copying a record's URL or updating a value across selected rows, without opening each form
questions.explain: The context menu lets a user act on rows directly from the list — useful for bulk updates without opening many forms.

questions.q: If a colleague's Incident list "looks different" from yours, what should you check first, per this lesson?
options: Whether you're each using a different named list view, not whether the underlying data differs
Whether their incident table has been deleted
Whether incidents are a different data type on their instance
Whether their instance is a different ServiceNow version entirely
questions.explain: Different columns almost always mean different named views of the same records, not different data.
